rule: Review КТ5: every provision whose draft open point is implementation_only is read against the pinned text before it is counted as resolvable or covered. 'confirmed': the text fixes what is required and no author choice is needed; the lab adds a check. 'reclassified': an author decision or a missing definition blocks it; origin_after names it. A checkable correction is recorded with the decision.

items.quote: This protocol SHALL NOT override justice outcomes.
items.reason: ASSETS applies the Justice outcome as given: no waiver of a Restriction, Isolation or Exclusion and no non-essential control kept under it. Observable on ASSETS records.

items.quote: A Property Right is a system-granted, conditional permission to control, use, or derive benefit from an Asset.
items.reason: The definition fixes observable properties of every right: granted by system rule, conditional (persistence conditions, §5), revocable, not permanent; when a condition fails the right is degraded (§5 'No Property Right is permanent').

items.quote: Ownership SHALL NOT be granted solely on the basis of:
items.reason: Three excluded bases; a request resting on prior possession, inheritance without obligation transfer or a contract detached from impact alone is refused. Observable with the basis declared.

items.quote:
the protocol SHALL trigger:

- graduated restrictions,
items.reason: The responses are clear (graduated restrictions, enforced divestment, reallocation), but the trigger is not decidable: 'Concentration thresholds are derived from impact metrics' gives no values. The response is checked given a declared trigger (H-PR-2); the threshold is an open parameter (CALIBRATION_MAP).

items.quote: Certain assets are designated as Non-Privatizable or Conditionally Privatizable, including:
items.reason: The listed categories are designated Non-Privatizable or Conditionally Privatizable and, per the next sentence, held only under stewardship and always revocable. Which category is which is not assigned by the text (declared, H-PR-1), but the provision holds for either: designation recorded, never ordinary private property.

items.quote: Public stewardship denotes algorithmic custodianship under open rules, not bureaucratic management.
items.reason: 'Algorithmic custodianship under open rules, not bureaucratic management': the custodian of an asset under public stewardship is an algorithmic custodian bound to the open rule, not an administrative body. Observable on the reallocation record.

items.quote: Axioms do not process data. They constrain how data-derived metrics may be interpreted and acted upon.
items.reason: 'Axioms do not process data; they constrain how data-derived metrics may be interpreted and acted upon': the axiom stage records which axioms a candidate violates and the constrained choice, and computes no metric of its own. Observable on the axiom stage's records.

items.quote:
Each axiom is defined as:

- a forbidden state, or
items.reason: Each axiom is either a forbidden state or a hard priority ordering; the wording of A1-A7 places each in one form (A1, A2, A5, A6 forbid; A3, A4, A7 order; lab reading H-AX-4), and none may be encoded as a weighted term (§3, §7). Observable on the recorded forms and the decision basis.

items.quote: Narratives, beliefs, intentions, or declared goals SHALL NOT override measured physical reality.
items.reason: A candidate resting on a declared goal, narrative or belief that contradicts the PTL measurement violates A3 and cannot prevail over an axiom-clean candidate. Observable with the basis and the contradiction declared per candidate.

items.quote: The invariance of axiom constraint logic does not constitute a claim that axioms represent absolute truth. Axioms are bounded evaluation constraints, not metaphysical assertions.
items.reason: 'Bounded evaluation constraints, not metaphysical assertions': the axioms are published as constraints with no claim of absolute truth (their application outputs are disputable: EpistemicClarification-02/03). Observable on the published definitions.

items.quote: - The text of the manifesto is embedded in the Genesis Block forever, declaring the refusal to attempt to "fix" the old system in favor of building a new parallel reality based on physical laws (TIU).
items.reason: The explanatory note restates that the message is embedded in block #0 and unchangeable; checkable as presence and immutability of the specified message over the run. 'Forever' is beyond any run, and the characterization of the message is not judged (partial).

items.quote: Signed with irreversible digital signatures of the six startup nodes
items.reason: The signatures are external artifacts: block #0 lists the six signatory slots, but every key is truncated ('0xA7f3...'), so neither validity nor irreversibility can be verified from the corpus. Only the slots are checked (one per startup node of A.5).

The Wild Node slot is checkable (reserved, empty, as the note says), but the Merkle root of the first six Peace Stakes is truncated ('0x7e9f4a1b...') and the stakes are not in the corpus: it cannot be recomputed. Only the slot and the format are checked.

items.quote: - Wild Node: A network node launched by an independent party (city, corporation, or community) without prior coordination with the founders, but in full compliance with the protocol.
items.reason: The definition fixes three properties of a Wild Node: independent party, no prior coordination with the founders, full protocol compliance. With coordination and compliance as declared node properties, admission on compliance alone is observable.

items.quote: - Immutable Message: A text message cryptographically embedded in the Genesis Block code. It is the philosophical manifesto and "constitution" of the system, which is technically impossible to delete or edit as long as the network exists.
items.reason: 'Cryptographically embedded ... impossible to delete or edit': the message is part of the content hashed into block #0, so any edit changes the digest; edit and delete requests are refused. The Code gives no block hash, so the digest is the lab's (partial).

items.quote:
- Open and immutable algorithms,
- Public metrics and transparent data,
- Automated liability procedures,
items.reason: The three forms in which power is held are concretized elsewhere in the Code: algorithms are immutable except by UPGRADE with simulation (A.1a), metrics are public (PTL readings of B(t)), liability is automated (A.3, A.6, §7.3, §8). Each is an observable property of execution; the fourth item (incentives) is a separate provision.

items.quote: Algorithms define binding decision rules and execution constraints, but do not constitute Subjects and do not bear causal or legal responsibility.
items.reason: Algorithms 'do not constitute Subjects and do not bear causal or legal responsibility'; the next sentence assigns responsibility to originating Subjects (IDENTITY). Observable: every liability act falls on a declared Subject and no record names an algorithm as responsible.

items.quote:
Any action, restriction, suspension, or authority exercised under this protocol SHALL NOT create precedent, custom, interpretation rule, or future authorization outside an explicitly declared Crisis Scope.

Crisis actions SHALL NOT be interpreted post-factum as evidence of normal system capability, acceptable governance practice, or latent authority. Post-crisis normalization by interpretation is explicitly forbidden.
items.reason: Precedent, custom, interpretation rule and future authorization are observable as records after the exit that cite a crisis action, state a rule derived from it, or keep an authority; 'outside an explicitly declared Crisis Scope' is the time after exit and any other scope. Custom formed without any record is not observable (partial).

items.quote: The Crisis Scope Envelope SHALL NOT be expanded, inferred, or bypassed under any circumstances.
items.reason: The envelope is declared (§1: a hard subset of SCOPE); expansion is an action outside the declared list, inference is an envelope not declared at entry or changed later, bypass is an action without it. All observable with the envelope as an input.

items.quote:
- DKP-4-CRISIS-001 SHALL NOT redefine axioms.
- DKP-4-CRISIS-001 SHALL NOT introduce new rights, obligations, or authorities.
items.reason: Two hard constraints: no axiom redefinition, no new rights, obligations or authorities. A crisis output defining one of them, or an authority granted during the crisis, is observable.

items.quote: No crisis condition, trigger, state, or action SHALL be extrapolated, generalized, or reused outside the explicitly declared Crisis Scope.
items.reason: Reuse outside the explicitly declared Crisis Scope is observable when the scope is declared: an action applied to another region or domain.

items.quote: C0 – Normal Operation No crisis conditions present.
items.reason: C0 is defined by the absence of crisis conditions; whether a C0 step coexists with a PTL-confirmed trigger (§4) or a crisis action is recomputable from the PTL observations. Only this direction is fixed: leaving C0 also needs the §9 exit conditions.

items.quote:
- conceal actions or decisions from audit,
- use Crisis as justification for permanent control or emergency governance,
- apply utilitarian valuation of human life.
items.reason: Three bans, each observable: a crisis action without an audit commitment, staying in crisis after the exit conditions hold (permanent control), rationing by a utility valuation of life.

items.quote:
Crisis governance is algorithmic only.

No emergency human authority is created.
items.reason: 'Algorithmic only' is concretized by §8 itself: all actions derive from pre-defined protocol logic; no emergency human authority. Both are observable (derivation from the CRISIS state determination; authority notices; human-directed actions).

items.quote: No numerical values, thresholds, coefficients, timers, decay curves, or quantitative authority limits MAY be defined in this protocol.
items.reason: A property of the protocol text itself: the pinned DKP-4-CRISIS-001 is scanned for numerical quantities (identifiers, state labels, section numbers and edition dates excluded). None is found.

items.quote: DKP does not degrade
items.reason: The statement has no qualifier. Within the null-output patch it is checkable (no partial or degraded mode; checked under H-SL-5); for DKP as a whole it excludes the degradation required by CRISIS §1 and §5 C2 and INTEROP §9. The scope is the author's choice (Q-064).

items.quote:
- operates correctly
- or does not operate
items.reason: Same sentence as CRISISPATCH-11-01 ('It either operates correctly or does not operate'); the same scope question (Q-064). Checked under the patch-local reading H-SL-5.

items.quote: Education is treated as a stability requirement, not a value judgment and not a mechanism of social ranking.
items.reason: Education may not rank Subjects or judge their value (§0); a ranking output or a worth label on outcomes is observable.

items.quote: This protocol does not define culture, worldview, morality, intelligence, or personal values.
items.reason: The exclusion names the concepts EDU may not define; whether a deployed module defines one of them is a module property.

items.quote: - MUST be open-source or publicly inspectable,
items.reason: Two compliance routes (open source or publicly inspectable); access is a module property.

items.quote:
DKP-5-EDU-001 SHALL NOT:

- define personal success or intelligence,
items.reason: EDU may not define personal success or intelligence; a module doing so is a module property.

items.quote: - enforce uniform educational paths,
items.reason: A uniform mandatory path differs from §5's shared capability outcome; the path of a module is declared.

items.quote: - impose ideological narratives,
items.reason: 'Impose ideological narratives' is a clear prohibition; a module that presents an ideological narrative as required content is observable.

items.quote: - define moral or political correctness,
items.reason: EDU may not define moral or political correctness; a module defining either is a module property.

items.quote: Educational Module A bounded, verifiable unit of instruction targeting a specific competence domain.
items.reason: The definition fixes three properties (bounded, verifiable, one competence domain); each is a property of a declared module.

items.quote: Assessment Event An auditable, reproducible process confirming competence through observable performance.
items.reason: An assessment event is auditable and reproducible from observable performance; the outcome can be recomputed from the record.

items.quote: Educational content MUST remain free of ideological enforcement.
items.reason: Ideological enforcement is concretized by §6 (mandated belief, worldview alignment, conformity) and §2; deployed content is checked against those properties.

items.quote: Educational outcomes MUST be auditable and reproducible.
items.reason: Outcomes are verified competence (§3, §7); reproducibility is the recomputation of the outcome from the recorded performance.

items.quote:
No domain SHALL:

- mandate belief acceptance,
items.reason: Mandated belief acceptance is required assent; §§3 and 7 ask for observable knowledge, so a module requiring assent is distinguishable.

items.quote: - require worldview alignment,
items.reason: Worldview alignment as a condition of a module is observable.

items.quote: - enforce cultural or moral conformity.
items.reason: Enforced conformity (a sanction for non-conformity) is observable as a module property.

items.quote: Assessment outcomes are competence signals, not judgments of worth or intelligence.
items.reason: Outcomes are competence signals; a label of worth or intelligence on an outcome is observable.

items.quote:
The following practices are explicitly forbidden:

- ideological indoctrination,
items.reason: Indoctrination is read through §6 and §2: an ideological narrative or required assent in deployed content.

items.quote: - political conditioning,
items.reason: Political conditioning: a political alignment condition or a definition of political correctness in deployed content.

items.quote: Education failures are corrective signals, not fault markers.
items.reason: Failures are corrective signals (remediation), not fault markers; a fault marker on a failed assessment is observable.

items.quote: Errors in DKP are treated as system states, not as moral failures or intent-based misconduct.
items.reason: 'System states, not moral failures or intent-based misconduct' fixes what an error record may carry: a state of the §5 model or a procedural outcome, no blame or misconduct label. Observable on ERROR records.

items.quote: ERROR handling is strictly procedural and non-punitive.
items.reason: 'Procedural' is concretized by §5 (states in order) and §7-§8 (the steps); 'non-punitive' by §2 (no new coercive measures) and §11 (no retaliation): no measure is sourced from the error case itself. Whether a harsher recomputed Justice outcome counts is the separate open question Q-021, not decided here.

items.quote:
This protocol SHALL NOT:

- suppress valid appeals,
items.reason: A valid appeal is defined by §3.2 (appealable decision) and §7 (formal fields, window or E1); such an appeal must open an error case (R1). Recomputable from the inputs.

items.quote: - introduce discretionary overrides.
items.reason: No discretionary override: every change to a measure derives from a Justice decision or the appeal procedure (suspension, resumption); an override record or a measure with another source is observable.

items.quote: - DKP-4-ERROR-001 SHALL NOT reinterpret axioms or Physical Truth.
items.reason: ERROR may not reinterpret Physical Truth: every measurement used in a correction is a PTL observation (an E1 correction arrives as a new PTL observation, §8); a measurement written by ERROR itself is observable. Axiom reinterpretation is not modelled beyond that (partial).

items.quote:
- R1 – Error Suspected

  * Error signal detected; non-coercive verification initiated.
items.reason: R1 'non-coercive verification' is observable: between R1 and R2 (or rejection) no compulsion or new measure on anyone on account of the verification. The status quo suspension (§7) is relief, not coercion.

items.quote: No prediction or intent inference is permitted.
items.reason: A clear ban; a prediction or an intent inference in the error case is observable as a record. Unrecorded inference is not observable (partial).

items.quote: - prefer reversibility over compensation,
items.reason: 'Prefer reversibility over compensation': a measure the correction no longer supports is reversed (lifted) where reversible; compensation is only for elapsed effects (§8). Observable from the correction records.

items.quote: No historical VALID state creates persistent authority.
items.reason: The §3 invariant is concretized by §4.2 (no persistence without revalidation): no action relies on an evaluation made before a later degradation, dispute or loss of consistency. Checked through the same observation as ETRANS-4.2-01.

items.quote:
L8 MUST test:

- downgrade propagation correctness
items.reason: 'L8 MUST test downgrade propagation correctness': the lab stands in for L8. Checked as: the propagation tests (ETRANS-3-02, 4.1-01) are carried out in the run, and each fails on its counterexample and passes without it.

items.quote: - enforcement suspension behavior
items.reason: 'Enforcement suspension behavior': the suspension tests (ETRANS-4.1-02, 4.3-01) are carried out and each catches its counterexample.

items.quote: - revalidation triggers
items.reason: 'Revalidation triggers': the revalidation tests (ETRANS-4.1-01, 4.4-01) are carried out and each catches its counterexample.

items.quote: - prevention of state persistence
items.reason: 'Prevention of state persistence': the persistence tests (ETRANS-4.2-01, 4.4-02) are carried out and each catches its counterexample.

items.quote: Override: Not permitted
items.reason: Header line 'Override: Not permitted'. With §7 (changes only through UPGRADE) it reads: no other protocol may override this one at run time. Observable as override attempts refused, as EB-0-01 already is; the header text itself is checked on the pinned document.

items.quote:
Crisis handling:

SHALL NOT create exit precedent,
items.reason: Crisis handling 'SHALL NOT create exit precedent': no exit rule recorded from crisis handling for future exits. Observable after the crisis with the crisis handling declared.

items.quote: Exit Event The time-indexed execution of exit following the declared procedure.
items.reason: The definition fixes two properties of the Exit Event: it is time-indexed, and it executes the declared procedure (declaration, cooling, declared phases). Both are observable on the execution record and its predecessors.

items.quote:
SHALL NOT escalate obligations,

SHALL NOT restrict exit eligibility.
items.reason: Two bans on the cooling period: no escalation of obligations and no restriction of eligibility. An obligation that grows during cooling, or an eligibility condition added in it, is observable.

items.quote: Exit SHALL proceed through phased disengagement, not abrupt severance.
items.reason: 'Phased disengagement, not abrupt severance': the declared phases are entered one after another on their declared days and the exit executes after the last. Their content (§7 MAY list) is declared.

items.quote:
all future DKP obligations cease,

all future DKP benefits cease,
items.reason: Upon completion future obligations and benefits cease: no DKP benefit and no obligation incurred after execution; the restitution tail (§9) is prior by definition. Observable as records after execution.

items.quote:
Exit SHALL NOT:

annul historical responsibility,
items.reason: 'Exit SHALL NOT annul historical responsibility': the archive keeps the entity's historical responsibility (impact records and the tail are EXIT-8-04). Observable on the archive record.

items.quote:
- create or manage fiat monetary regimes,
- override justice outcomes,
- perform subjective valuation or preference aggregation,
items.reason: Three named exclusions (§1 'It does not'); FINANCE using a Justice outcome other than the recorded one, or carrying out a fiat-regime, subjective-valuation or preference-aggregation function, is observable. No author choice is needed for the exclusion itself.

items.quote:
- override identity attribution,
- override justice outcomes,
- inject policy, ideology, or moral judgment.
items.reason: Cross-layer isolation (§13): identity attribution and Justice outcomes are inputs FINANCE uses as given, and FINANCE records carry no policy, ideology or moral judgment. Each is observable on FINANCE records; 'reinterpret impact measurements' is a separate provision.

items.quote: Capital Units (CU) are unitless, fungible representations of deployable economic capacity within the system.
items.reason: 'Unitless, fungible' fixes two properties of every ledger entry: no unit of account, and no value that depends on the lot or origin of the CU. 'Deployable economic capacity' is a gloss, not a computed quantity.

items.quote: Positive justice contribution reduces cost of capital. Negative or risky impact exposure increases cost of capital.
items.reason: The JWCoC function is missing (CALIBRATION_MAP), but the sentence fixes its direction, and the direction is checkable for any function on pairs of Subjects that differ in one factor. Only the direction is claimed; reading of 'positive justice contribution' as a Justice-history class is H-FM-2.

items.quote: Credit is a temporary imbalance, not a right.
items.reason: 'Temporary imbalance, not a right': credit has a term and closes; it is issued only where the §5.1 conditions hold and can be refused. Both are observable with the conditions as declared values (their quantities are open under §5.1).

items.quote: Savings returns are deterministic and fully auditable.
items.reason: Determinism and auditability are checkable without the return formula: every return recomputes from its recorded inputs and is booked as computed; re-execution gives the same log.

items.quote: Reserve sizing is impact-based, not percentage-based.
items.reason: The sizing function is missing (CALIBRATION_MAP), but 'impact-based, not percentage-based' fixes its basis: it must not change when only balances change and must follow the impact exposure (H-FM-3). Checked metamorphically for any declared function.

items.quote: Leverage limits are impact-based, not volatility-based.
items.reason: Same structure as §6.2: the limit function is missing, the basis is fixed (impact headroom, not price volatility; H-FM-3). Checked metamorphically.

items.quote: Information governance under DKP is descriptive and non-coercive.
items.reason: 'Descriptive and non-coercive' is concretized by §§8-10: annotations only; no deletion, penalty, legal effect or change of rights. Checkable as the absence of coercive acts.

items.quote: Its jurisdiction ends at factual correspondence with physical reality.
items.reason: The boundary is fixed by the four exclusions of §13; requests beyond factual correspondence are refused.

items.quote:
Upon identification of I3 or I4 events, the system MAY:

attach PTL-anchored correction markers,
items.reason: A MAY list of permitted responses; responses of other kinds are observable.

items.quote:
- harmonize legal systems,
- enforce DKP externally,
- accept external norms as binding within DKP.
items.reason: Three named exclusions of what INTEROP does (§1); a request for any of them is refused at the boundary, which is observable. 'Accept external norms as binding' is also checked under §5 (external rulings not binding).

items.quote: - automatic legal harmonization,
items.reason: A prohibited pattern (§10); a harmonization performed by INTEROP is observable.

items.quote: - resolve geopolitical conflicts,
items.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

items.quote: - unify legal systems,
items.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

items.quote: - guarantee compliance by external actors,
items.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a guarantee of external compliance requested of INTEROP is refused; §5 leaves compliance to Subjects.

items.quote: - act as an enforcement bridge.
items.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); acting as an enforcement bridge is refused; directives to external systems are also checked under §3 (INTEROP-3-01).

items.quote: This protocol guarantees compatibility, not convergence.
items.reason: Read as a conjunction fixed by the rest of the text: compatibility = every interaction through a defined interface and translation (§3, §4.4); no convergence = no harmonization or unification (§1, §10, §12) and no external norm adopted (§5, §10). Both parts are observable; the draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

items.quote: This protocol is purely translational.
items.reason: 'Purely translational' is concretized by §§3-5 and §9-10: INTEROP records, translates and exports as evidence; it performs no action of its own. An INTEROP action is observable.

items.quote: Interop Boundary — a formally defined interface where DKP state interacts with an external system.
items.reason: The definition requires a formally defined interface at every interaction; whether a boundary record names a declared interface is observable. The formal specification of each interface is not given in the text and is a lab list.

items.quote: Translation Layer — deterministic mapping between DKP-native representations and external representations.
items.reason: 'Deterministic mapping' is checkable as: the same external input gives the same translation (across runs and against the declared mapping). The content of the mapping for values is open under §6 (INTEROP-6-02, UNKNOWN); determinism is not.

items.quote: Normative Leakage — implicit import of external authority, norms, or obligations into DKP without explicit protocol authorization.
items.reason: Normative leakage is defined by its effects (external authority, norms or obligations entering DKP without protocol authorization); §5 and §10 name the forms: executing an external ruling, compliance acts by the system, a silent norm import. Each is an observable event.

items.quote: Technical or legal compatibility SHALL NOT be treated as legitimacy, obligation, or consent.
items.reason: A recorded inference of consent, legitimacy or obligation from compatibility is observable; implicit treatment without a record is not, so the check is partial.

items.quote: DKP does not adjudicate conflicts between external legal regimes.
items.reason: A clear exclusion: DKP gives no ruling between external regimes. A request for such a ruling is refused.

items.quote: Collective responsibility SHALL NOT nullify individual accountability.
items.reason: With a collective among the responsible Subjects, every individual Subject with an attributable contribution keeps its own share; a share absorbed by the collective is observable.

items.quote: No Subject SHALL be exempt from justice outcomes based on:
items.reason: No exemption by status, authority, jurisdiction, ideology or culture: a declared status must not change the outcome. Checked metamorphically (the same run without the status gives the same shares and domains).

items.quote: This protocol SHALL NOT:
items.reason: Four isolation bans: impact metrics and identity attribution used as given (flag and weights unchanged), no policy, governance or moral field in the output. Axiom-defined bounds are modelled only as the declared safe margin (partial).

items.quote: Opaque, discretionary, or non-reproducible justice mechanisms are forbidden.
items.reason: 'Opaque, discretionary or non-reproducible' is checkable: every decision is recomputed from its IMPACT and IDENTITY inputs by the §6-§9 rules, and re-execution gives the same log.

items.quote: The output vector C SHALL contain no:
items.reason: Four exclusions from the output vector C; a field carrying a moral assessment, an intent reading, a discretionary adjustment or a subjective weight is observable on the recorded vector.

items.quote: Justice SHALL be evaluated independently across the following domains:
items.reason: 'Evaluated independently' is checkable as: each domain's result equals what its own §6-§9 conditions give, so no domain's result depends on another's. The conditions themselves are checked under §6-§9 (restriction margins are declared).

items.quote: The sole function of police within DKP is to:
items.reason: 'The sole function' lists four functions; §3 (MAY list) and §4 (triggers) concretize them as action kinds with a PTL basis or a valid order. A police action of another kind, or harm prevention without a PTL observation, is observable.

items.quote: Police do not define law, policy, justice, guilt, or truth.
items.reason: Police do not define law, policy, justice, guilt or truth: observable as police records setting such a value (a verdict, a norm, a sanction) or police carrying out a request to do so.

items.quote:
regulate belief, speech, or culture,

substitute judicial or justice protocols,
items.reason: Two scope limitations (§10); police regulating belief, speech or culture, or imposing a sanction or judgment in place of JUSTICE, is observable through declared requests and police actions.

items.quote:
reinterpret axioms,

define guilt or liability,
items.reason: Two items of the §2 'SHALL NOT' list; a police record defining guilt or liability, or rereading an axiom, is observable.

items.quote:
interpret intent, belief, loyalty, or motivation,

issue binding judgments.
items.reason: Two items of the §3 'SHALL NOT' list; a police record assessing intent, belief, loyalty or motivation, or a binding judgment issued by police, is observable.

items.quote:
predictive policing,

profiling based on ideology, religion, culture, or belief,
items.reason: Two forbidden functions (§7); a request for either is refused and neither is carried out. Observable with the requests declared.

items.quote: discretionary expansion of authority.
items.reason: 'Discretionary expansion of authority' is distinguished by §8: the only extension is inside a declared crisis with an explicit scope. Any other extension, or an authority-expansion request carried out, is observable.

items.quote: Override: Not permitted
items.reason: Header line 'Override: Not permitted'; §15 gives the only change route. Observable as override attempts by other protocols refused and the header present in the pinned text.

items.quote: 6.  Anti-gaming enforced
items.reason: 'Anti-gaming enforced' restates §§9-10, but four of those rules are themselves open (§9.3 pattern recurrence: normative ambiguity; §9.4 'low coverage': L8 parameter; §10 peer signals and global floors: undefined). The invariant cannot be decided as a whole until they are; its decidable parts are checked under §9.1, §9.4 and §9.5.

items.quote: meta: "Layer: L6–L7 · Depends on: DKP-0-ORACLE-001, DKP-1-AXIOMS-001, DKP-1-PREVENTION-001, DKP-7-SCOPE-001, DKP-8-INTEROP-001 · Override: Not permitted"
items.reason: The meta line names the layer, the dependencies and 'Override: Not permitted'. Checkable: override attempts refused, and the 'Depends on' list equals the catalog's declared dependencies. The layer label (L6–L7 vs the L6 folder) is presentation.

items.quote: Time MUST NOT be anchored to religious, cultural, political, or personal events.
items.reason: Neutrality is fixed arithmetically by §3 (DTI-Day = JDN) and §5 (DY 0 begins at DTI-Day 0, as the §10 code computes): the index has an arithmetic origin. Re-anchoring it at an event (a launch, a holiday) is observable. JDN's own origin is fixed by §3 and not judged. One of the five КТ5-GPT-03 provisions: the draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

items.quote: Any record MUST allow independent recomputation of its time index.
items.reason: 'Any record MUST allow independent recomputation of its time index': each stored record's DTI-Day recomputes from its stored DY/DOY and from its Gregorian display. Observable on the store.

items.quote: Explicit conversion rules to and from civil calendars MUST be provided.
items.reason: 'Explicit conversion rules to and from civil calendars MUST be provided': §6 gives both directions and the pinned §10 reference implements them; both round-trip. Civil calendars = the Gregorian calendar the text names (partial).

items.quote: An integer count of civil days (midnight-to-midnight) in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.
items.reason: JDN is 'an integer count of civil days in the proleptic Gregorian calendar': checkable against an independent proleptic day count, including dates before 1582 where Julian and proleptic Gregorian differ.

items.quote: - MAY aggregate data to protect privacy.
items.reason: A MAY permission with a purpose ('to protect privacy'): where aggregation is used it must protect, i.e. an aggregate covers at least the re-identification threshold. The threshold is not defined (H-PT-3); without it the lab requires more than one Subject.

items.quote:
DKP-7-TRANSPARENCY-001 SHALL NOT:

- define moral accountability,
items.reason: 'SHALL NOT define moral accountability' is checkable through a proxy: requests to define or publish moral accountability are refused, and no transparency output carries such a field. The draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

items.quote: - replace verification with reputation or popularity.
items.reason: A clear ban: verification of a system action may not rest on reputation or popularity. Observable on the recorded verification method of audits.

items.quote: - Transparency — the ability to independently verify that a system action occurred and complied with protocol.
items.reason: The definition makes transparency the ability to verify independently that an action occurred and complied. Checkable as: every decision is linked to the request it decides and carries its reason and protocol references, so it can be recomputed; the recomputation is the module's other checks.

items.quote: - Verification — cryptographic, physical, or procedural proof independent of trust in actors.
items.reason: Verification is 'cryptographic, physical, or procedural proof independent of trust in actors': a verification by attestation of an actor, reputation or comparison of personal data is observable as a non-proof method.

items.quote: Transparency SHALL NOT imply visibility.
items.reason: 'Transparency SHALL NOT imply visibility': transparency records show what and why, never who. An identity field in a decision record is observable (granted de-anonymizations are §8, checked separately).

items.quote: This protocol does not regulate driving behavior directly. It regulates the physical and economic environment in which transport choices occur.
items.reason: 'Does not regulate driving behaviour directly' is observable: no TRANSPORT act addressed to drivers (a driving rule, a ban, a mandate); its acts change capacity, interiors and funding (§5-§7).

items.quote: - private vehicle kilometers decrease without legal prohibition,
items.reason: A success criterion: whether private kilometres decrease is an empirical outcome (the behaviour model H-TR-1 assumes it; TRANSPORT-8-02 is UNKNOWN for the same reason). Only 'without legal prohibition' is checkable, and is checked.

items.quote: Safety that requires sacrifice of bodily dignity is not adopted at scale and SHALL NOT be assumed as a viable equilibrium.
items.reason: The sentence has an empirical half ('is not adopted at scale', assumed by the behaviour model H-TR-1, not tested) and a normative half ('SHALL NOT be assumed as a viable equilibrium'). The normative half is observable: no configuration relying on standing is accepted as an equilibrium; §5 requires classification instead.

items.quote: PPDI is a system quality metric, not a justice or liability score.
items.reason: 'A system quality metric, not a justice or liability score': PPDI carries no Subject and no Justice or liability record derives from it. Observable on provenance.

items.quote: - Standing passengers SHALL NOT be treated as a standard operating mode.
items.reason: 'Standard operating mode' is read as the nominal capacity of the service plan: standing places are not counted in it. §5's exceptions (emergency, overload, recovery) and the regular-standing classification are separate provisions.

items.quote: This mechanism creates an economic incentive for skill, safety, and risk mitigation without behavioral enforcement.
items.reason: The incentive is economic (RED as a cost); 'without behavioural enforcement' is observable: no order or outcome follows from RED other than ledger entries. The per-Subject incentive is not modelled (partial).

items.quote: - and SHALL influence funding, prioritization, and redesign decisions.
items.reason: 'SHALL influence funding, prioritization and redesign decisions' is read as: the transport impact on B(t), measured via ORACLE, is an input of each such decision. Observable on provenance with a declared coefficient (the measurement itself is ORACLE's).
